newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lamfalussy sees rates behind dollar rise - Stark.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy sees rates behind dollar rise - Stark.

text.p: European Monetary Institute president Alexandre Lamfalussy sees interest rate differentials between the U.S. and Europe as the main reason for the dollar's recent strength, German state secretary for finance Juergen Stark said on Monday.
Stark briefed reporters on Lamfalussy's presentation to a meeting of European finance ministers. Stark attended the meeting in place of German finance minister Theo Waigel.

Long-term interest rates in Europe have fallen to their lowest levels in 30 to 40 years, while strong economic growth has boosted rates in the U.S. Long-term rates in Germany, for example, have dropped to 5.81 percent, while in the U.S. they are 6.37 percent, he said.
"We have succeeded in decoupling European interest rates from U.S. rates," Stark said. "This decoupling is also a factor in the higher valuation of the U.S. dollar."

Lamfalussy characterised European monetary policy as cautious and appropriate, and said it had generated credible market expectations of lower long-term interest rates and a flattening of the yield curve, Stark said.
Lamfalussy said many of the economic problems facing Europe, including high unemployment, were structural, and should not stand in the way of further budget consolidation.
